A Texas university law professor suffered a heart attack in the middle of class — before being rescued by his students, including a Navy SEAL veteran, whom he has credited for saving his life.

Michael Maslanka, a 73-year-old associate professor, was delivering a lecture at the UNT Dallas College of Law when he ominously told his students he might not be able to continue before suddenly blacking out on Oct. 6.

“I just saw blackness,” the longtime litigator told the university Tuesday.

Students sprang into action when Maslanka collapsed.

Among the students who rushed to his aid was third-year student Matthew Melton, a Navy SEAL veteran who had previously taught CPR classes while serving in the US Special Forces.

Melton, who was previously deployed to Bahrain in 2001 and Iraq in 2005, trained with the 18 Delta medics and field surgeons who worked to save lives on the battlefield.

The 45-year-old said his past experiences in conflict zones taught him to “always be able and ready to pivot and always be open to what might happen.”

“Students were freaking out. Action needed to be taken,” he told the law school.

Melton, who is training to become a lawyer, performed three rounds of CPR on the professor but he was still not out of the woods.

“He came back. Then he went out [of consciousness] again. I was going from chest compressions to forced air [in his mouth]. When I did the first compression, I could hear his ribs break.”

Maslanka shouted when he regained consciousness — but was unaware of his surroundings, according to the veteran.

“He thought his life was about to be extinguished. He didn’t know where he was,” Melton said.

While Melton, a cybersecurity professional, worked on the law prof, Sanchez, who lost her dad to a heart attack two years ago, turned to prayer.

“Everyone was bawling,” she said of the frightening ordeal.

Maslanka experienced an abnormal heart rhythm known as ventricular tachycardia — a condition where the upper and lower chambers of the heart go out of sync.

He regained consciousness and spent 11 days recovering in the hospital, crediting the students for saving his life, comparing his near-death experience to a crossroads.

“I had one that night. Life or death,” he said, before paying tribute to his students.

“They knew what to do. They organized themselves intuitively. And that saved my life. Let me just be clear,” he told WFAA.

“I would not be here today if my students did not act quickly, thoughtfully and responsibly. I would be dead. They saved my life.”

It has since emerged that 12 years ago the professor appeared in a Texas Bar program titled “Mike Maslanka @ your desk” – where he actually encouraged his students to “think like a SEAL.”

He’s also written an article entitled “Four Life Hacks That Dying (Twice) Taught Me,” which will be published in the Texas Lawyer publication.

Maslanka, who first joined the university in 2015, has since made a return to the law college – teaching ethics and employment law.
news.content:
پوشش های بیشتری را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. یک استاد حقوق دانشگاه تگزاس در وسط کلاس دچار حمله قلبی شد — قبل از اینکه توسط دانشجویانش، از جمله یک سرباز کهنه سرباز نیروی دریایی SEAL، که او را به خاطر نجات جانش معرفی کرده است، نجات یابد. مایکل ماسلانکا، دانشیار 73 ساله، در حال ایراد سخنرانی در کالج حقوق UNT دالاس بود که به طرز شومی به دانشجویانش گفت که ممکن است نتواند ادامه دهد قبل از اینکه ناگهان در 6 اکتبر خاموش شود. قاضی قدیمی دادگاه سه شنبه به دانشگاه گفت: "من فقط سیاهی دیدم". در میان دانش‌آموزانی که به کمک او شتافتند، متیو ملتن، دانشجوی سال سوم، سرباز نیروی دریایی SEAL بود که قبلاً در حین خدمت در نیروهای ویژه ایالات متحده، کلاس‌های CPR را تدریس کرده بود. این مرد 45 ساله گفت که تجارب گذشته اش در مناطق درگیری به او آموخته است که "همیشه قادر و آماده چرخش باشد و همیشه در برابر آنچه ممکن است رخ دهد باز باشد."
او به دانشکده حقوق گفت: "دانشجویان بهم ریخته بودند. باید اقداماتی انجام شود." ملتون که برای وکیل شدن آموزش می بیند، سه دور CPR را روی استاد انجام داد اما او هنوز از جنگل بیرون نیامده بود. "او برگشت. سپس دوباره [از هوشیاری] خارج شد. من از فشار سینه به هوای اجباری [در دهان او] می رفتم. وقتی اولین فشرده‌سازی را انجام دادم، می‌توانستم صدای شکستن دنده‌هایش را بشنوم.»

A 122-year-old Illinois building partially collapsed Wednesday, injuring at least three people – hours after an entire building in Brooklyn disintegrated, killing eight.

The facade of the structure in Aurora, Ill., crumbled down onto the street as pedestrians and cars raced out of the way of the debris cloud, according to video obtained by Fox 32 Chicago.

The building, located on the 100 block of East Galena Boulevard, suffered a partial collapse at around 6:37 p.m. as part of the exterior wall fell, taking with it the scaffolding structure, city officials said.

Three people sustained minor injuries during the collapse and are expected to “make a full recovery,” officials said, without providing additional information on their location at the time of the destruction.

Dozens of cars had been traveling along the adjacent Broadway street that houses several restaurants and stores in the popular downtown section of the city.

A car had pulled out of a street parking spot and begun driving away as a portion of the building fell into its path along the street, forcing the driver to swerve out of harm’s way.

A cloud of smoke enveloped the street as the part of the city came to a standstill.

The building was evacuated as a precaution and crews performed a controlled collapse using “targeted water operations” to remove “structurally unsound” portions of the building.

City officials closed down the streets outside the building until it was deemed structurally sound and the scaffolding was repaired.

A cause of the collapse was not known but investigators pointed to the surveillance video that captured the roof of the building falling, taking the exterior wall and scaffolding with it.

A large chunk of the upper floor and roof was missing in aftermath photos provided by the city that showed the complete destruction left behind by the collapse.

Initial evidence from the scene did not link Wednesday’s collapse to a similar incident at the same address in 2025, where a part of the building’s brick facade fell onto the nearby train tracks.

The historic building – built in 1904 – was mostly empty, consisting of vacant apartments with only one store, a barber shop, currently operating on the first floor, according to property records viewed by The Post.

Wednesday’s collapse came three and a half hours after a three-story apartment building fell in Flatbush, Brooklyn.

The collapse, which occurred at around 4 p.m. Eastern on 1321 Flatbush Avenue, killed eight people – including two children – and sent 18 others to the hospital.

The doomed New York building had separated from the rest of the structure, falling into an excavated construction pit.

Dozens of residents were displaced as city officials vacated three neighboring buildings until engineers determined if they were structurally sound to house people again.

A stop-work order had been issued by the Department of Buildings in March after inspectors discovered violations at the construction site next door, including inadequate overhead protection such as netting and sheds to shield neighboring buildings.
news.content: اطلاعات بیشتری از پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. یک ساختمان 122 ساله در ایلینویز روز چهارشنبه فروریخت و حداقل سه نفر را مجروح کرد - ساعتی پس از فروپاشی کل ساختمان در بروکلین و کشته شدن هشت نفر. شیکاگو این ساختمان که در بلوار 100 بلوار گالن شرقی واقع شده است، حدود ساعت 18:37 دچار ریزش جزئی شد. مقامات شهری گفتند که بخشی از دیوار بیرونی سقوط کرد و ساختار داربست را با خود برد. مقامات گفتند که سه نفر در جریان ریزش جراحات جزئی داشتند و انتظار می رود "به طور کامل بهبود یابند." ده‌ها خودرو در امتداد خیابان برادوی مجاور که چندین رستوران و فروشگاه را در بخش محبوب مرکز شهر در خود جای داده‌اند، در حال حرکت بودند. وقتی قسمتی از ساختمان به مسیر خود در امتداد خیابان سقوط کرد، یک خودرو از پارکینگ خیابان خارج شد و شروع به حرکت کرد و راننده را مجبور کرد از مسیر آسیب‌دیده منحرف شود. ابری از دود که قسمتی از شهر را فراگرفته بود. ساختمان به عنوان یک اقدام احتیاطی تخلیه شد و خدمه با استفاده از "عملیات آب هدفمند" برای حذف بخش‌های "سازه‌ای ناسالم" ساختمان یک فروریختن کنترل شده انجام دادند. مقامات شهر خیابان‌های خارج از ساختمان را بستند.

news.originalContent:
Heavy rains flood shelters, damage solar power systems and threat essential healthcare services.

Deir el-Balah, Gaza Strip – As the rain intensified, 65-year-old Abu Sajed rushed to place buckets and pots strategically around his modest room in central Gaza.

The stone walls and tarpaulin roof offered little protection to his makeshift home, east of Salah al-Din Street, near the “Yellow Line” in Bureij refugee camp.

“We could no longer stay in bed because of the heavy rain. We moved to chairs in the only part of the room the water had not reached and waited for the rain to stop,” said Abu Sajed, who has diabetes.

He searched for his blood glucose monitor in the darkness. But it was soaked and no longer working.

His family’s solar power system, used for lighting and charging phones, was also damaged. Water also flooded his daughter’s neighbouring tent, soaking her clothes and belongings and destroying the inverter connected to her solar system.

“I did not know what to do. I could not protect myself or my family. Even going to the toilet had become difficult because of all the water,” he said.

His ordeal continued after the rain stopped. The following morning, as he tried to leave the room, his foot slipped on the muddy floor and he fell. Because of poor health, he could not get up alone. His wife and daughter struggled to lift him.

“I felt helpless and exhausted,” he said.

Recent rainfall has added to Gaza’s suffering, and due to Israel’s siege, most people lack adequate housing.

But the impact extends beyond flooded shelters and damaged belongings. It also threatens the energy sources residents depend on, particularly amid Gaza’s continuing electricity crisis.

In a room inside a damaged building in northern Gaza, Mohammed al-Hour uses sunlight to charge people’s phones through his solar power system. But rainwater also seeps through the cracked walls and damaged ceiling of his room.

“People come to me asking to charge their phones, even for a little while, so they can have lighting at night. But when the clouds persist and the sun disappears, it becomes difficult,” he said. “Whether you live in a tent or a house, rainwater will find its way in. The bombardment has destroyed almost everything.”

Companies trying to maintain electricity services are struggling with the damage.

Despite preparations in advance of the winter, Abu Zayed Electricity Company could not prevent water from entering several facilities, damaging equipment and causing generators to malfunction. It temporarily suspended services at affected branches over fears of electrical contact and short circuits.

Aya Shaheen, the company’s general manager, said distribution panels and electricity metres were covered with plastic sheeting and tarpaulins, exposed wires were insulated, and municipalities were asked to pump out accumulated water. But the damage exceeded available resources.

“However much we try to prepare and protect our equipment, we continue to face major obstacles because of the extensive destruction of infrastructure,” she said. “Municipalities are also dealing with enormous pressure. Flooded tents need urgent intervention, so they cannot respond to every request for assistance.”

Water entered one of the company’s sites, even though its generators are housed in specially equipped prefabricated structures, Shaheen said. Restoring services and repairing equipment can take hours or days, depending on the damage.

According to UNICEF, the recent rainfall affected more than 106,000 people. About 950,000 displaced people live in flood-prone areas, including 400,000 in particularly high-risk locations.

A joint assessment by the World Bank, the United Nations and the European Union estimated that 80 percent of electricity generation and distribution assets had been destroyed or rendered inoperable during the war. This has severely limited access to reliable electricity, particularly as solar generation declines on cloudy days and equipment becomes vulnerable to water damage.

Mohammed Abu Khaled, an engineer specialising in energy systems and equipment used in the health sector, warns that rainwater entering solar systems can damage batteries and inverters, causing short circuits and corrosion of electronic circuits.

“The inverter is the weakest link and the component most likely to fail. It contains sensitive electronic circuit boards that are often not adequately protected against water,” he said.

He estimated that malfunctions in household solar systems and those used in displacement camps increased by more than 40 to 50 percent following recent rainfall. Repairing a damaged inverter can cost between $200 and $500, while families may have to replace an entire battery if it is damaged.

Solar panels’ electricity output can also drop by 60 to 80 percent on cloudy days, slowing battery charging and reducing the hours households can rely on stored electricity, he added.

The risks become more serious when rainwater reaches hospital equipment, particularly as many health facilities have been forced to operate from prefabricated structures and temporary buildings offering inadequate protection against the weather.

Abu Khaled said strong winds and heavy rainfall can cause water to seep into hospital departments, exposing operating-room equipment, portable oxygen generators, vital-signs monitors, laboratory devices and lighting systems to moisture and damage.

Some equipment has already been affected by damp conditions, adding pressure to healthcare facilities struggling with severely limited resources, he said.

As rainfall continues, Gaza’s residents face another winter with little infrastructure to protect them and few resources to replace damaged belongings and equipment.

With water seeping into shelters, electricity systems at risk of failure and medical equipment increasingly vulnerable, the weather is adding another burden to families struggling to maintain the most basic conditions for survival amid the destruction.
news.content: باران‌های شدید پناهگاه‌ها را سیل می‌کند، به سیستم‌های برق خورشیدی آسیب می‌رساند و خدمات بهداشتی ضروری را تهدید می‌کند. دیرالبلاح، نوار غزه - با شدت گرفتن باران، ابوساجد 65 ساله با عجله سطل‌ها و گلدان‌ها را به‌طور استراتژیک در اطراف اتاق ساده‌اش در مرکز غزه قرار داد. دیوارهای سنگی و دیوارهای سنگی و سقف برزنتی کوچکی از خانه‌اش را به صلاح می‌سازد. خیابان، نزدیک «خط زرد» در اردوگاه آوارگان بوریج. ابوساجد که دیابت دارد، گفت: «به دلیل باران شدید دیگر نمی‌توانستیم در رختخواب بمانیم. به سمت صندلی‌هایی در تنها قسمتی از اتاق که آب به آن نرسیده بود حرکت کردیم و منتظر ماندیم تا باران بند بیاید.» او در تاریکی به دنبال دستگاه سنجش قند خون خود گشت. اما خیس شده بود و دیگر کار نمی کرد. سیستم انرژی خورشیدی خانواده او که برای روشنایی و شارژ تلفن استفاده می شد نیز آسیب دید. آب چادر همسایه دخترش را نیز غرق کرد و لباس‌ها و وسایل دخترش را خیس کرد و اینورتر متصل به منظومه شمسی را از بین برد. او گفت: «نمی‌دانستم باید چه کار کنم. نمی‌توانستم از خودم یا خانواده‌ام محافظت کنم. حتی رفتن به توالت هم به دلیل این همه آب سخت شده بود.» مصیبت او پس از قطع باران ادامه یافت. صبح روز بعد وقتی می خواست از اتاق خارج شود، پایش روی زمین گل آلود لیز خورد و افتاد. به دلیل وضعیت نامناسب، او نمی توانست به تنهایی از جای خود بلند شود. همسر و دخترش برای بلند کردن او تلاش کردند. او گفت: «احساس درماندگی و خستگی می‌کردم.» بارندگی‌های اخیر بر رنج غزه افزوده است و به دلیل محاصره اسرائیل، اکثر مردم کمبود کافی دارند.

news.originalContent:

An Arizona couple was arrested after allegedly stabbing a registered sex offender to death in a desert area of the state, according to authorities.

Jacob Middlebrook, 35, and his girlfriend, Layne McIntosh, 36, were initially taken into custody for second-degree homicide in the death of 29-year-old Arron Christopher Warren, Bullhead City Police said on social media.

Police began investigating after a motorist found a dead man on the side of the road in the 3100 block of Silver Creek Road on Saturday.

The circumstances surrounding the man’s death appeared suspicious, so detectives were called to the scene to conduct a homicide investigation.

Detectives later identified the man as Warren, a Bullhead City “transient.”

Detectives also identified a possible suspect and discovered that the victim’s vehicle was missing.

Hours later, Las Vegas Metro Police assisted Bullhead City investigators and located the victim’s vehicle parked at a casino in Laughlin, Nevada.

Middlebrook and McIntosh were taken into custody by Las Vegas Metro Police and booked into the Clark County Detention Center in Las Vegas, where they will be held until they can be extradited to Mohave County, Arizona.

On Monday, the pair’s charges were upgraded to first-degree homicide.

Investigators determined that the two were also “local transients” who had known the victim for the past few months.

“Detectives discovered that the couple had expressed distaste for registered sex offenders and had planned the homicide in advance,” Bullhead City police said.

“The couple reportedly pre-determined the desert location where they intended to leave Warren’s body. They also reportedly measured furniture/beds that could be large enough to cover the victim’s body along the side of the road. Warren was a registered Level 2 sex offender,” the post added.

Bullhead City Police Chief Paul George said the department updates the community when certain registered sex offenders move in or change addresses but that he “will not tolerate anyone using this information as a reason to threaten, intimidate, harass or harm another person.”

“When a Level 2 or Level 3 sex offender moves into our area or, more commonly, changes addresses, the Bullhead City Police Department shares that information as a public service to help keep residents informed,” he said in a statement. “While required notifications are mailed to residents living within an approximate 1,000 feet radius of an offender’s registered address, we go a step further by sharing these notifications on social media to reach a broader audience. Our goal is to provide information, not create fear or alarm. We believe an informed community is a safer community.”

“Our Bureau of Criminal Investigations conducts monthly address verification checks to help ensure registered sex offenders are complying with registration requirements. Our responsibility is to protect our community, keep residents informed and to enforce the law. We take all three of these seriously,” George continued.

news.originalContent:

Needle & Skein, a yarn shop in Minnesota, apologized last week for selling “Harry Potter”-themed kits, calling the decision a “mistake.”

“We recently sold Harry Potter-themed kits, and we owe you a sincere apology,” the business wrote on Facebook Saturday.

“I’m a mom, and I read these books aloud to my child. Those evenings are some of my sweetest memories, and I think that warmth kept me from stopping to consider what carrying this merchandise would mean for our trans friends, neighbors, and customers. I made a mistake, and I’m so sorry,” the statement continued.

“Harry Potter” author JK Rowling has faced criticism in recent years over her opposition to policies allowing transgender women into certain female-only spaces.

In an essay last month, Rowling doubled down on her stance, calling transgender activism “elitist to its core.”

The store announced that it had removed the “Harry Potter” items from the shelves and donated all the proceeds to Point of Pride, an organization that provides support to transgender people.

“We never meant to hurt anyone. But we can see that we did, and we are truly sorry to everyone who felt less welcome in a space that should always feel like home to you. You deserve better from us,” the company said.

Needle & Skein also shared an image showing its donation to Point of Pride, saying it donated three times the profits from its “Harry Potter” merchandise. The business also shared a link for followers to donate.

Needle & Skein told Fox News Digital that the response to its apology had been largely positive, despite some doxxing and negative reviews.

“Overall, the response has been positive, with people feeling that we were open, honest and appreciative,” owner Gilah Mashaal said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Rowling for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

Rowling has also faced boycott efforts from LGBTQ activists targeting her books and merchandise. Last year, a San Francisco bookstore announced that it would no longer be selling Rowling’s books due to her views on gender.

Christian Toto, host of the “Hollywood in Toto” podcast, told Fox News Digital that he doubted the owners of the Minnesota yarn shop understood exactly why Rowling’s views were controversial.

“The media blurs many facts in our culture, like how ‘immigration’ isn’t separated into two distinct camps — legal and illegal. Something similar likely is happening here. And for a yarn hobbyist to take such a stand is, well, the height of silliness on too many levels to count. Sadly, she’s far from alone,” Toto said.
news.content:
موارد بیشتری از پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. Needle & Skein، یک فروشگاه نخ در مینه‌سوتا، هفته گذشته به دلیل فروش کیت‌های با مضمون «هری پاتر» عذرخواهی کرد و این تصمیم را «اشتباه» خواند.
این تجارت شنبه در فیس بوک نوشت: «ما اخیراً کیت هایی با مضمون هری پاتر فروختیم و یک عذرخواهی صمیمانه به شما مدیونیم.» «من یک مادر هستم و این کتاب ها را با صدای بلند برای فرزندم خواندم. آن شب‌ها از شیرین‌ترین خاطرات من هستند، و فکر می‌کنم این گرما باعث شد که فکر نکنم حمل این کالا برای دوستان، همسایه‌ها و مشتریان ترنس ما چه معنایی دارد. من اشتباه کردم و خیلی متاسفم.» جی کی رولینگ، نویسنده «هری پاتر» در سال‌های اخیر به دلیل مخالفتش با سیاست‌هایی که به زنان تراجنسیتی اجازه می‌دهد در فضاهای خاص زنانه حضور داشته باشند، با انتقاداتی مواجه شده است. رولینگ ماه گذشته در مقاله ای موضع خود را دو چندان کرد و فعالیت تراجنسیتی را «تا هسته خود نخبه گرایانه» خواند.
این فروشگاه اعلام کرد که اقلام «هری پاتر» را از قفسه‌ها حذف کرده و تمام درآمد حاصل از آن را به Point of Pride، سازمانی که از افراد تراجنسیتی حمایت می‌کند، اهدا کرده است. «ما هرگز قصد صدمه زدن به کسی را نداشتیم. اما می‌توانیم ببینیم که این کار را انجام دادیم، و واقعا متاسفیم برای همه کسانی که در فضایی که همیشه باید احساس می‌کردند که خانه شماست، کمتر از آن استقبال کردند. شما سزاوار بهتری از ما هستید.» این شرکت گفت. Needle & Skein همچنین تصویری را به اشتراک گذاشت که کمک مالی خود را به Point of Pride نشان می‌داد و گفت که سه برابر سود حاصل از کالای «هری پاتر» خود را اهدا کرده است. این تجارت همچنین پیوندی را به اشتراک گذاشته است.

A highly contagious strain of bird flu has struck a backyard poultry flock in Wisconsin, prompting officials to euthanize the birds amid ongoing concerns about the spread of the potentially deadly disease.

The Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection (DATCP) confirmed Thursday a case of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) in a backyard poultry flock in Rusk County.

Officials did not specify how the flock became infected.

DATCP said all birds on the property were euthanized and will not enter the food system.

HPAI, a highly contagious virus that is often fatal to domestic poultry, has circulated among wild and domestic birds in North America since December 2021, according to DATCP.

The disease is caused by influenza type A viruses and can vary in severity depending on the strain and affected species.

The virus can spread through contact with infected birds, wild birds or their droppings, as well as contaminated equipment or clothing worn by people working with the animals, according to DATCP.

When HPAI is confirmed in a backyard poultry flock, officials may establish a 10-kilometer surveillance zone, though surrounding poultry premises would not face movement restrictions.

DATCP urged livestock owners to take precautions to protect their flocks and herds, including washing hands, disinfecting equipment, restricting access to animals and separating new additions for at least 30 days.

The agency also recommended that poultry owners keep their birds indoors when possible.

news.originalContent:
Outlook, Teams and Copilot remain disrupted in 74 countries as Microsoft reports ‘marginal success’ in fixing outage.

Microsoft says it has had only “marginal success” in restoring its most widely used workplace services, more than 12 hours after a global outage knocked out Outlook and disrupted Teams and Copilot for users in 74 countries.

In a statement on its service health page early on Friday, the company said it was monitoring activity across regions to assess server status and find ways to improve capacity. “This includes reviewing server performance and confirming that developed patches have been applied and working as intended after infrastructure reboots are completed,” it said.

Here is what we know about the outage, what caused it and when services might return.

Problems with Microsoft products began at about 16:00 GMT on Thursday, when users began reporting that they could not access Outlook, its email platform. Within about an hour, the outage tracker Downdetector had logged reports from 74 countries and territories.

Microsoft first said it was investigating problems in the Americas, but later confirmed that users in any region could be affected. It said the affected infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which was likely contributing to the connectivity errors.

The company later said a number of servers had become unexpectedly unavailable, and that the elevated load had not been caused by an increase in traffic.

The disruption dragged on through the US working day and into the night. By Friday morning in Europe, it had still not been resolved, and servers Microsoft had restored were failing again.

“I don’t think it’s unprecedented. I mean, the scale is impressive,” Rupert Goodwins, a technology analyst and journalist, told Al Jazeera “It’s very embarrassing for Microsoft and really, really annoying for the rest of us.”

Microsoft has not confirmed the number of users who have been affected.

Data from Downdetector, through which users can report problems with online services, gives a partial picture, however.

At about 07:00 GMT on Friday, it had received at least 43,000 reports of problems with Outlook from users in 72 countries. The true number is likely far higher, since the figure only counts people who visit the site to report an issue.

“There’s about 430 million people who use Microsoft services,” said Walter Pasquarelli, an affiliate researcher at the Bennett School of Public Policy at the University of Cambridge and an AI specialist. “What we do know so far is that this is first and foremost a communication risk.”

Government systems in Singapore and Japan have been disrupted, as have communications at the Supreme Court of the Philippines. In Australia, the country’s spy agency and federal police were among the organisations hit.

Outlook has been hit hardest. Users have reported being unable to open their mailboxes via the web, the app or through mobile devices, and many emails which do go through have arrived late.

Other services have been partly disrupted. The disruption has spread beyond Microsoft’s own products, hitting integrations which other companies, including the AI firms OpenAI and Anthropic, rely on.

“For the most part, we don’t really think about it too much, a little bit like our health, that we kind of take these tools for granted until they’re suddenly down or they’re not there,” Pasquarelli said.

Microsoft has not published a root cause but said the outage was not the result of a cyberattack.

On Friday, it was rolling back a network change, but did not say if that change was to blame for the problems.

“We will continue to share more information as soon as we have it, and for now I can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity,” Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, said in a post on X late on Thursday.

Australia’s Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said Microsoft had also told him it did not believe it was dealing with a cyberattack. “They believe they are dealing in some ways similar to what we saw with respect to CrowdStrike where there is an update that has gone awry,” Burke told a news conference in Sydney.

Goodwins said elevated load usually comes from one of two places. “Either there’s an external attack and some aggressor is trying to put lots and lots of artificial loads on the system to break it,” he said. “Microsoft says that hasn’t happened, and I believe them because there are ways to mitigate that.”

The other common cause, he said, is a faulty update to internal systems. “The update gets sent out over the administration network to all these servers, but there’s a mistake, and instead of it fixing things, it makes them reset or stop being able to talk to each other,” he said.

Pasquarelli said the evidence so far points to a technical failure. “It could literally be like a cable that basically damaged some of the infrastructure. It could be a sign of basically incompetence. It could be a mistake on some of their automated systems,” he said. “So far I do not see any evidence that points to an extremely high amount of computational power or traffic that is caused by AI systems.”

Goodwins said Microsoft’s focus on AI may have played an indirect role. “Microsoft has been completely focused on AI, and I imagine that the stuff like email and Teams, they’re just seen as forgotten revenue source. They won’t have got the investment and thought and management mind space they should have done,” he said.

“It does also show that for all Microsoft’s AI, it hasn’t got any AI that can help fix the networks,” he said.

Microsoft has posted a series of updates on X about the progress it is making to restore service. Late on Thursday, it reported only limited recovery as it tried to route users’ traffic away from affected servers, and later said the changes it had applied were not taking effect as expected.

“Some of these servers basically started failing some automated health checks, and then the traffic would go to some of the other servers, and they would then get overloaded,” Pasquarelli said.

“Think of it a bit like a highway where you have four lanes, and now all of a sudden you have two lanes. That means that there’s a lot more traffic, and because there’s traffic, then the entire thing shuts down,” he said.

Goodwins said servers knocked offline usually attempt to reconnect so they can synchronise their files again. “As things come back up, they’re immediately swamped by the traffic from all the other servers desperate to talk to them. So it all falls down again,” he said.

“When the traffic accident’s cleared, there’s gridlock. There’s a huge backlog of traffic, and the roads can’t cope with it,” he said.

Goodwins also said many experienced engineers have left Microsoft. “It’s not so much that there aren’t enough human eyes, but all the experienced people, the people who built the stuff up, have left,” he said. “There’s been a draining of corporate memory of how these systems are built up and how they work.”

Microsoft has not given a timeline for full recovery. It has said that as capacity returns, users may see service come back gradually as their apps reconnect, rather than all at once.

“It’s fairly early on in the story. We don’t know all the facts,” Goodwins said. “It’s been going for a long time, and Microsoft’s been quite open in the fact the fixes aren’t really working yet.”

There is little users can do themselves, as the problem lies with Microsoft’s servers rather than their own devices. The desktop version of Outlook may still show emails already downloaded, while Teams chats and calls have largely continued working.

Goodwins said the short-term impact of such outages tends to be limited. “You can’t log on to your email for a bit. Well, that happens all the time because your broadband’s down or your local computers stop working,” he said. “It comes back up and you grumble a bit and get back on with life.”

Pasquarelli said organisations should plan for such disruptions. “What is the minimum viable service or the minimum viable product that we need to keep up if there’s a global outage?” he said.

This is not Microsoft’s first major outage this year. In January, Microsoft 365 went down across North America for almost 10 hours. The company blamed that on heavy service load combined with reduced capacity during maintenance.

In late August, thousands of Outlook users worldwide were locked out of their mailboxes.

Other tech companies have suffered similar failures. In October 2025, an Amazon Web Services outage took down a large number of websites and apps.

In July 2024, a faulty software update from the cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike crashed computers around the world, cancelling flights, disrupting hospitals and causing billions of dollars in losses.

The outage comes as Europe pushes for greater technological sovereignty, aiming to run its own servers and depend less on foreign providers. Lacking tech giants of its own, the continent relies heavily on US firms for digital services.

That push has gained momentum during US President Donald Trump’s second term, as he has imposed tariffs on Europe and threatened to take over Greenland, a Danish territory.

Earlier this year, French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said government officials would stop using Zoom and other US-owned video conferencing tools in favour of French software, partly to reduce “dependencies on non-European actors”.

“With the whole thing about digital sovereignty, meaning that you can’t trust that your data is secure if it’s being served by an American company because of changes to US legislation, certainly in Europe, there have been big pushes to find alternatives to Microsoft, and this sort of thing will only increase the pressure,” Goodwins said.

He added that Microsoft has relied on “intensive inertia”. “People feel they have to stick with Microsoft because the pain of transitioning somewhere else is too great. But at some point, that pain threshold changes,” he said.

Goodwins said he did not expect an immediate impact on Microsoft’s revenue, because customers are tied into licensing contracts. “I think in the long term it probably will, but in the short term, and it’s quarter-by-quarter business here, it won’t,” he said.

Pasquarelli said he could envisage a short dip in Microsoft’s shares, but that its dominance of office software would be hard to replicate. “I don’t think that there’s any firm, at least not in Europe, that because of this outage could provide a credible and solid alternative,” he said. He added that organisations are more likely to “focus more on their digital resilience instead of building something of their own”.

A lightsaber used by Darth Vader in the “Star Wars” movies “The Empire Strikes Back” and “Return of the Jedi” sold Thursday for nearly $5 million in an auction.

The lightsaber, which was used in the climactic duel in Cloud City where Vader tells Luke Skywalker “I am your father,” sold for $4.875 million at the Ultimate Star Wars Auction held by Heritage Auctions.

The sale marks a world auction record for any “Star Wars” collectible, according to Heritage Auctions.

The sale also established a new auction record for a screen-used “Star Wars” prop, according to the auction organizer, shooting past their $3.75 million July auction sale of Skywalker’s lightsaber and severed hand-effects rig from “The Empire Strikes Back.”

Heritage’s Thursday auction also featured material from “Star Wars” Episodes I through IX and additional films and TV shows.

In addition to Vader’s lightsaber, 27 other “Star Wars” lightsabers were assembled for public auction, according to Heritage Auctions.

news.originalContent:
A look back at the Global South's early efforts to challenge Western dominance of international news.

Daya Thussu was still a student when he landed a subediting desk job at the Press Trust of India (PTI), then India’s largest news agency.

It was the early 1980s, and the newsroom in New Delhi was alive with the clatter of telex machines delivering dispatches from across the world.

At his desk, Thussu, then in his mid-20s, worked through two very different streams of international news. One came from established Western agencies, including Reuters. The other arrived through a little-known network connecting newsrooms across Asia, Africa and Latin America.

“We would check the ticker to see what the story was and where it had come from,” Thussu says of his work with the Non-Aligned News Agencies Pool (NANAP). “It could be from anywhere - the Philippines, Iraq or across Africa. My job was to select stories that we would then send out to the PTI wires.”

The two streams of news offered different windows on the world. One came from established international agencies, largely based in Western capitals. The other represented an attempt by countries long dependent on those agencies to tell their own stories.

Describing it as a cumbersome process in which copy was edited by hand and then given to a typist to put into the system, Thussu nevertheless remembers it as valuable training. “It was great hands-on training for someone like me who was very interested in international news and was pursuing a PhD in international relations at Jawaharlal Nehru University,” he says from his home in London.

For decades, a handful of Western news agencies had dominated the flow of international reporting. Now, countries that had fought for political independence were trying something else: exchanging news directly with one another without relying on London, Paris or Washington, DC, to tell their stories.

It was an experiment born of the Non-Aligned Movement, a coalition of countries seeking a path independent of the rival superpowers of the Cold War.

And it raised a question that remains pertinent today: Who decides what the rest of the world gets to know?

By the mid-19th century, three European news agencies had emerged as dominant players in the international news business: Germany's Wolffs Telegraphisches Bureau, Britain's Reuters and France's Agence Havas, the predecessor of Agence France-Presse (AFP).

In 1859, the three agencies struck agreements dividing international news markets and territories between them, helping determine which stories circulated around the world and where.

“It was a news cartel system,” Thussu says.

Such was the power of these agencies that Reuters, founded in 1851 during the height of the British Empire, is often referred to in scholarly circles as “an empire within an empire”.

Through its use of telegraph networks and agreements granting it exclusive rights to collect and distribute news across much of the British Empire, Reuters built an international reach closely tied to Britain's imperial infrastructure.

But as colonial empires began to unravel in the 20th century, newly independent nations started questioning why the flow of international news remained so heavily concentrated in Western hands.

In 1955, representatives of 29 Asian and African countries gathered in Bandung, Indonesia, to discuss cooperation and a shared future beyond colonial rule. Six years later, the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) was formally established in Belgrade in then-Yugoslavia. It brought together countries seeking an independent path amid the Cold War rivalry between the United States and Soviet Union.

Among the leaders associated with its founding were Yugoslavia's Josip Broz Tito, India's Jawaharlal Nehru, Egypt's Gamal Abdel Nasser, Ghana's Kwame Nkrumah and Indonesia's Sukarno.

During a 20th century that saw a series of wars across the world, an end to the British Empire and the growth of US imperialism, NAM was initially a loose structure that would grow to include nations that included Fidel Castro’s Cuba and Muammar Gaddafi’s Libya.

By the time the OPEC oil embargo hit in the early 1970s, the growing alliance would become more structured in its approach.

Sima Kokotovic, a scholar specialising in global communication at the University of Pennsylvania, says the movement began taking more concrete steps towards a framework for sustainable cooperation among its members at its conferences in Lusaka, Zambia, in 1970 and Algiers, Algeria, in 1973.

As NAM countries pushed for greater self-reliance, they increasingly questioned the role of mass communication and “how much it was being controlled and dominated by the media companies from the West and, to a degree, the Soviets”.

For countries that had won political independence, the question was increasingly whether they could also tell their own stories, and challenge the way they were represented to the rest of the world.

The Non-Aligned Movement became the home of debates about imbalances in the international system whether economic or cultural or information.

“The Non-Aligned Movement became the home of debates about imbalances in the international system whether economic or cultural or information,” Thussu explains.

These discussions would feed into a wider campaign for a New World Information and Communication Order (NWICO), debated within UNESCO.

Its supporters wanted developing countries to build stronger news agencies, broadcasting infrastructure and direct channels for exchanging information to reduce their dependence on Western media organisations.

Speaking to Al Jazeera from Beirut, Lebanon, Nabil Dajani, now 89, recalls the optimism surrounding those early efforts.

From 1971 to 1975, he served as a member of UNESCO’s International Panel of Experts on Communication Research and remembers feeling both energised and overwhelmed by his role on a panel that, for the first time, was addressing these issues on an international stage.

Dajani, an emeritus professor of media studies at the American University of Beirut, remembers NWICO as an ambitious, if idealistic, attempt to address inequalities in the global flow of information.

“The Non-Aligned countries believed that the wealthy Western nations had imposed information imperialism on them, which was essentially a form of neocolonialism. Their argument was that the major international news agencies reported on developing countries only when disasters, wars, diseases and other negative events occurred,” he says.

“So the underlying principle was that information is not merely a commodity but a fundamental human right.”

Today, Thussu is a senior research fellow at the Institute of Commonwealth Studies at the University of London. He has contributed extensively to global debates about information flows and imbalances throughout the decades that followed his time at PTI, including cowriting the 1992 book Contra Flow in Global News: International and Regional News Exchange Mechanisms.

“It wasn’t just about the flow of information one way; it was about a two-way flow with this idea about horizontal communication between nations sharing similar struggles,” he says.

“Brazilians who were reading or watching news about the Philippines, for example, were getting information mediated through London or New York and vice versa. ... This was about people knowing more than just the bad politics but about culture, individuals and day-to-day life, which were often ignored in Western media coverage.”

The debates were taking shape during a turbulent decade marked by wars in Southeast Asia and the Middle East, liberation struggles in Africa and military dictatorships in Latin America. By the mid-1970s, NAM countries were beginning to put their ambitions for a more equitable flow of information into practice.

In January 1975, a statement by Sri Lankan Prime Minister Sirimavo Bandaranaike was transmitted by telex across participating news agencies from Yugoslavia’s Tanjug news agency to others across the Global South, heralding NANAP's official launch.

Ljubica Markovic was 24 years old when she started working at Tanjug, the former Yugoslav state media outlet founded by Tito in 1943, which is still in existence today. Markovic worked closely with the designated NANAP news desk during her time on the foreign desk.

Unlike most communist states in Eastern Europe, Yugoslavia was not aligned with the Soviet Union. Its independent position during the Cold War and its leading role in the Non-Aligned Movement made it a natural champion of cooperation between countries seeking alternatives to Western and Soviet influence.

“There was a great deal of enthusiasm for international media cooperation, largely as a result of Yugoslavia’s position in the world at the time,” Markovic, today a 78-year-old grandmother living in Belgrade, tells Al Jazeera.

“With a strong media infrastructure in place, Tanjug was best placed to play a central role in NANAP. It was the backbone of this initiative, but it was neither its centre nor its arbiter. It was a large network of agencies exchanging news, and Tanjug was one of these points, probably among the most active ones,” she says.

Recalling her two decades at Tanjug, she says everyone in the editorial unit had access to the pool’s concept and the news it handled.

At Tanjug, journalists prepared domestic stories for foreign audiences, shortening and translating them before sending them through the network by telex or radio link. The work differed from the foreign desk, which selected reports arriving from other agencies and correspondents for Yugoslav audiences.

“No one questioned the value of the idea of a more equitable exchange of information and culture.”

NAM’s vision for a more equitable global information system inspired further outlets and agencies, including Third World magazine, or Terceiro Mundo, in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Uruguayan-born journalist Beatriz Bissio cofounded the magazine in 1974 with a group of journalists, including her husband, the prominent exiled Brazilian journalist and politician, Neiva Moreira.

According to Bissio, Moreira was inspired to launch the magazine after attending the Non-Aligned Movement summit in Algiers the previous year.

Published in Portuguese, English and Spanish, the magazine reached a peak circulation of more than 150,000 copies in its Portuguese edition and remained active for more than three decades, Bissio says.

“Although the primary focus was on the coverage of Latin America, we always sought to offer readers information, analyses and historical perspectives on Africa and Asia as we were aware that our history and our destinies as Latin Americans were very closely related to those in these regions,” Bissio, who today works in the history department at the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro, tells Al Jazeera.

NANAP, she says, played an important role in bridging the information gap between Latin America and regions across the Global South.

Although Third World was not a news agency itself, it benefitted from the relationships NANAP helped foster. Bissio says the magazine built direct contacts with journalists and agencies across the Global South, particularly in countries such as Angola and Mozambique, exchanging reporting and gaining access to stories that rarely appeared in Western news coverage.

“Our challenge was to address issues such as the struggles against dictatorships and the fight for liberation in different parts of the world,” Bissio says.

“The mainstream media were not covering these issues, even stories as big as apartheid in South Africa were not known in Latin America. NANAP was really vital for us because it allowed us to have collaborators across many parts of the world.

"To have direct information through those agencies helped us diversify our coverage, and we were able to work with journalists with the same aims as us.”

The flow of information worked both ways, in particular, with the agencies in the newly independent Portuguese-speaking nations of Mozambique and Angola, which formed Agencia de Informacao de Mocambique and Agencia Angola Press (ANGOP) after their independence from Portugal in 1975.

“We met with the journalists from these agencies, formed agreements and exchanged articles. For them, covering Latin America was not easy, so they could take our coverage of Latin American countries and republish and redistribute it in their own way.”

Over a three-decade career with the magazine, Bissio interviewed key political leaders such as Fidel Castro, Nelson Mandela and Hugo Chavez, travelling extensively across Asia and Africa, including Angola and Mozambique, where she reported on the final stages of the liberation struggles.

She was also in the Middle East, reporting from Beirut in 1982 during Israel’s invasion of Lebanon, which was aimed at driving the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) out of the country.

These experiences, she says, profoundly shaped her understanding of liberation struggles across different regions.

“Witnessing firsthand the struggle of the Angolan and Mozambican people in such adverse conditions yet driven by very strong ideals of freedom and justice was a defining experience for me. As a Latin American, I had never witnessed people taking up arms and fighting by every means they have against a colonial army.”

Despite its challenges, NANAP expanded. By 1992, researchers estimate that nearly all 108 member countries of the Non-Aligned Movement were participating in the pool, including through agencies such as Cuba's Prensa Latina and Iraq's Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The volume of news exchanged also grew from an average of 8,000 words a day in 1975 to 40,000 in 1983 and 120,000 by 1992.

Yet the disparity with established international news agencies remained enormous. In 1978, the four dominant agencies - The Associated Press, United Press International, AFP and Reuters - were reported to produce a combined 33 million words a day.

Alongside Tanjug, India, particularly under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and PTI, also played a key role both within NAM and NANAP.

This gave Thussu good insight into the day-to-day challenges NANAP faced. “The majority of pool members were not English-speaking countries, so translation was a big consideration,” he recalls.

“Plus journalism standards varied across the countries. Some of my PTI colleagues used to hate the NANAP shift because they had to deal with copy that wasn’t always of a high standard.

"Despite debates around how Western news agencies accurately represent other cultures and whether context might be missing or distorted, factually, they would always be correct. And if there was a mistake, even a tiny one, they would immediately send a rejoinder, which wasn't the case with the NANAP copy.”

Very little NANAP copy made it into Indian newspapers. “Part of the problem was that most members of NANAP represented national news agencies, which were state-controlled,  whether of right-or left-wing orientation, and their copy was, more often than not, the official propaganda of the ruling party.”

The ambition soon extended beyond newswires. In 1977, two years after NANAP’s launch, NAM nations launched a broadcasting arm, the Broadcasting Organization of Non-Aligned Countries (BONAC), which was aimed at sharing radio and television broadcasts directly with one another.

Kokotovic explains that BONAC was a more ambitious initiative because its members were interested in developing the media infrastructure needed for international collaboration.

NAM countries organised conferences, training workshops and annual television and radio festivals, bringing together media workers in cities ranging from Havana, Cuba, to New Delhi and Freetown, Sierra Leone. The aim was to develop ways for countries to cooperate in producing and sharing news and information.

Among these efforts was 20 Years of Non-Alignment, a film coproduced by Cuban, Algerian, Indian and Yugoslav television broadcasters to mark the movement's 20th anniversary in 1981. Despite these initiatives, Kokotovic says BONAC faced significant internal and external challenges from the outset.

“There were many technical and structural issues, specifically since the shapes of media infrastructures were vastly different across all the different member countries. Circulating different programmes was just technically difficult, not to mention the issue of translation. Simply put, what was at stake is how expensive this all was.”

Analysts say it was these financial imbalances that posed the biggest threats to NAM’s vision around structural change because many NAM nations were economically dependent on the same Western powers they were seeking to gain autonomy from.

Markovic recalls how this imbalance played out for journalists working at the time.

In 1984, she attended a seminar in Tunis organised by Tunisia's national news agency, TAP, which brought together journalists from about 30 nonaligned countries. Funded by the US embassy, the seminar featured American lecturers, including representatives from The Associated Press who offered training in reporting standards and impartial journalism.

The training was valuable, Markovic remembers, but she also felt the lecturers were eager to demonstrate what journalists from nonaligned countries could learn from Western media practices.

Then something unexpected happened.

“At one point, ... a critical article about Western media and cultural imperialism began circulating among the participating journalists almost clandestinely,” she says.

With NAM growing from 25 founding nations to about 90 members in 1980, working as a monolithic entity also started proving difficult, and conflicts between NAM members, such as the Iran-Iraq War in the 1980s, started to impact the progress of the media projects.

Thussu recalls the difficulties he faced with the war coverage: “Every day we would get a lot of copy from IRNA in Iran and Iraq’s INA because they wanted to tell their side of the story, and there would be disparities in terms of numbers of people killed or injured and discrepancies with the details of the actual attack or defence.

"In the end, we ended up using transnational agencies because we knew that at least the basic facts were clear.

"The Iran-Iraq War was a striking example of what the problem with the pool system was, but there were many other cases of conflicts too. For example, in India, you wouldn't use the Pakistan agency copy,” he says, referring to Pakistan Press International (PPI), established in 1956.

In 1980, UNESCO published Many Voices, One World, a landmark report examining inequalities in international communication.

Produced by an international commission chaired by Sean MacBride, an Irish politician, diplomat and Nobel Peace Prize laureate, the report included contributions from figures such as Colombian writer and journalist Gabriel Garcia Marquez and Tunisian minister Mustafa Masmudi.

It exposed inequalities in the global flow of information, highlighting Western media dominance over Global South nations, media monopolies and commercialisation. It also called for a more just and balanced media economy.

As UNESCO’s director general, Senegalese educator Amadou-Mahtar M'Bow, argues in the report’s foreword: “It is essential that all men and women, in all social and cultural environments, should be given the opportunity of joining in the process of collective thinking thus initiated. …

"With the coming of a new world communication order, each people must be able to learn from the others, while at the same time conveying to them its own understanding of its own condition and its own view of world affairs. Mankind will then have made a decisive step forward on the path to freedom, democracy and fellowship.”

The backlash, however, was immediate and, as commentators have said, unsurprising.

Kokotovic explains that the report highlighted disparities in media infrastructure and the largely one-way flow of information. For the US and UK, however, its proposals were contentious. Both regarded the report as biased and argued that its approach risked imposing greater governmental control over the media.

“For their part, the Soviets were not overly pleased either.”

The United States withdrew from UNESCO at the end of 1984, followed by Britain at the end of 1985, depriving the organisation of substantial funding.

Bissio remembers the impact of these funding cuts. “The reaction of the US and of Great Britain, to put it simply, was just brutal. The funding cuts created a very serious problem for UNESCO, and it has never again tried to develop the idea of democratisation of media.”

The 1980s were a decade bookended by major events: Tito died in 1980, the Berlin Wall fell in 1989 and the Cold War was drawing to a close. Yugoslavia’s breakup followed in the early 1990s after years of mounting tensions. Amid these shifts, efforts with NWICO, NANAP and BONAC started to slowly dissolve.

The developments in Yugoslavia and changes with Tanjug, in particular, would directly impact BONAC. But as Kokotovic says, BONAC did leave a mark.

Kokotovic suggests that the international cooperation fostered through NAM's media initiatives may have helped influence how some governments later approached their own media industries.

In India, for example, the state had previously regarded the movie industry with suspicion. By the 1990s, however, it was increasingly embracing media and entertainment as industries that could boost the economy and project a positive image of the country internationally.

Kokotovic says some of the figures involved in BONAC initiatives during the 1970s and 1980s later played a role in changing perceptions of what the state's relationship with media industries could be.

The global news landscape also changed with the emergence of broadcasters based outside traditional Western media centres. Al Jazeera launched in 1996, and its English-language channel followed in 2006, reaching international audiences with reporting from the Middle East and beyond. As the network marks its 30th anniversary, the earlier debate over who gets to tell the world’s stories offers a wider historical context for that shift.

Al Jazeera has certainly made its presence felt in the global news space - and not just in the news-rich Middle East. Within the past couple of decades, it has also emerged as a credible and professional voice of the Global South.

“Al Jazeera has certainly made its presence felt in the global news space - and not just in the news-rich Middle East. Within the past couple of decades, it has also emerged as a credible and professional voice of the Global South,” Thussu says.

NANAP itself, meanwhile, had not disappeared entirely. Although its newswire operations had slowed, it was rebranded as the NAM News Network (NNN) in November 2005 and continues to operate today.

Journalists who worked during the earlier years say it was an important moment both on a personal level and for South-South transnational media cooperation.

“I had a very strong reporting experience in the Middle East when I covered the struggle of the Palestinians in the occupied territories and in Lebanon, where I covered people's struggles for justice and democracy," Bissio says.

"It wasn't the same, but there were parallels to what we as Latin Americans were dealing with under dictatorships, and these experiences helped me understand both my own and other struggles.”

She would go on to cofound the Serbian-based Beta News Agency and is today working on a book based on the testimonies of 17 journalists that documents how Tanjug was transformed during the 1990s from an internationally respected media outlet into what she says is an instrument of war propaganda.

She says that for her and some of her colleagues, the 1970s represented a time when they felt connected to the international community. “With the outbreak of war in Yugoslavia and the country’s breakup, NANAP gradually faded away. Nevertheless, it had undoubtedly helped ensure that global news coverage was not entirely one way at a time when technical means of communication were limited.

"During the pool’s expansion in the 1970s, their number was around 50. Most reports from what was then called the Third World and reports from Africa, Asia and Latin America written by Tanjug correspondents found their way into Yugoslav media. This opportunity gave Tanjug journalists a sense that they were participating in the global media scene.”

For Dajani, who witnessed the early optimism surrounding the nonaligned media movement, its ambitions remain relevant in an age when a handful of powerful technology companies increasingly shape how information is produced and consumed.

The technologies may have changed, but the underlying struggle over who controls information, whose stories are told and whose voices are heard remains unresolved.

Dajani believes revisiting that history, including its ambitions and shortcomings, could offer lessons for those seeking to build a more equitable global media landscape today.

“In today's digital age, new forms of imbalance have emerged: global monopolies in technology and media, widening digital divides and the silencing of voices from the margins. The muted fate of the new world information order reminds us that inequality in communication is not settled but an ongoing struggle.

"If this history is remembered and understood, it may yet inspire fresh initiatives, better informed and more resilient to confront the challenges of our time.”

نگاهی به تلاش‌های اولیه جنوب جهانی برای به چالش کشیدن سلطه غرب بر اخبار بین‌المللی. دایا توسو سو هنوز دانشجو بود که در Press Trust of India (PTI)، بزرگ‌ترین خبرگزاری هند در آن زمان، مشغول به کار شد. اوایل دهه 1980 بود و اتاق خبر در دهلی نو با صدای تق تق از دستگاه‌های تلکس ارسالی از سراسر جهان زنده بود. توسوسو که در آن زمان در اواسط 20 سالگی خود بود، پشت میز کار خود، دو جریان بسیار متفاوت از اخبار بین المللی را بررسی کرد. یکی از آژانس های معتبر غربی از جمله رویترز بود. دیگری از طریق یک شبکه ناشناخته که اتاق‌های خبری را در سراسر آسیا، آفریقا و آمریکای لاتین به هم وصل می‌کرد وارد شد. توسو در مورد کار خود با استخر آژانس‌های خبری غیرمتعهد (NANAP) می‌گوید: «ما تیکر را بررسی می‌کنیم تا ببینیم داستان چیست و از کجا آمده است». "این می تواند از هر جایی باشد - فیلیپین، عراق یا سراسر آفریقا. کار من انتخاب داستان هایی بود که سپس به سیم های PTI ارسال می کردیم."
دو جریان خبری دریچه های متفاوتی را به جهان ارائه کردند. یکی از آژانس‌های بین‌المللی مستقر عمدتاً در پایتخت‌های غربی بود. دیگری نشان‌دهنده تلاش کشورهایی بود که مدت‌ها به آن سازمان‌ها وابسته بودند تا داستان‌های خودشان را بگویند. با توصیف آن به عنوان یک فرآیند دست و پا گیر که در آن یک کپی با دست ویرایش می شد و سپس به یک تایپیست داده می شد تا در سیستم قرار دهد، با این وجود از آن به عنوان آموزش ارزشمند یاد می کند. news.originalContent:
The Banking Committee says the ex-tech CEO and the US commerce secretary could face legal action if they fail to appear.

United States lawmakers have summoned Nvidia’s former CEO Jensen Huang and US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify about their roles in the scandal rocking the tech company.

Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott on Thursday requested that they appear in a public hearing on December 3. He threatened that the pair would face subpoenas should they refuse.

Huang resigned earlier on Thursday amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman US authorities suspect of spying for China.

The firm, which manufactures advanced chips powering artificial intelligence, has since seen its market value fall below $4 trillion for the first time since July 2025.

Amid the scandal, President Donald Trump’s administration faces allegations that Nvidia did not receive proper scrutiny for its exports of advanced semiconductors to China.

Lawmakers have also accused Lutnick’s Commerce Department of refusing to add dozens of Chinese companies to a US trade blacklist.

“Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive U.S. technology,” Scott wrote in a post on X. “The American people deserve answers.”

Three other House committees have asked Huang and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter to appear for separate hearings on December 1 and 2, or face subpoenas.

Under Secretary of Commerce Jeffrey Kessler was summoned for a December 3 hearing.

In a joint letter, the head of the Foreign Affairs Committee, Brian Mast, China Select Committee Chair John Moolenaar, and House Intelligence Committee Chair Rick Crawford wrote that “there are clear national security concerns that need to be addressed immediately.”

China has denied allegations of spying on the US. President Trump earlier defended Huang, calling him “honourable”.

Senator Richard Blumenthal voiced concern to Al Jazeera over allegations that Nvidia had donated $25,000 to the Trump administration.

China on Friday warned that the tightening of US regulations on the export of semiconductors would threaten the stability of global industry and supply chains.

Bejing “has consistently opposed the abuse of export control measures,” a foreign ministry spokeswoman said.

Amid the Nvidia scandal, US lawmakers have called for limits on exports of chip equipment to China.

news.originalContent:
دونالد ترامپ در مصاحبه با هیو هویت، مجری محافظه‌کار آمریکایی، گفت برای استفاده دوباره از نیروی نظامی علیه ایران «هیچ تردیدی» ندارد و باقی ماندن حکومت کنونی ایران تا پایان ریاست‌جمهوری خود را «شکست» می‌داند.

این دو موضع، در کنار اعلام بی‌نیازی واشنگتن از توافق با تهران، پرسش درباره هدف نهایی آمریکا و چگونگی پایان جنگ را به محور پوشش رسانه‌های آمریکایی تبدیل کرده است.

واشنگتن‌پست و آکسیوس، دستور آقای ترامپ به جی‌دی ونس برای تمرکز بر مسائل داخلی را نشانه عقب‌نشینی از مسیر توافق و ترجیح ادامه فشار اقتصادی توصیف کرده‌اند؛ بلومبرگ نیز این رویکرد را شرط‌بندی بر دوام وضعیتی شکننده می‌داند و هشدار می‌دهد پذیرش بن‌بست، لزوماً به پایان درگیری یا رفع خطر جنگی تازه منجر نخواهد شد.

دونالد ترامپ در مصاحبه با هیو هویت، استفاده دوباره از نیروی نظامی علیه ایران را منتفی ندانست. آقای هویت پرسید آیا برای جلوگیری از تهدید متحدان و کشتی‌های آمریکایی تردید خواهد کرد؛ آقای ترامپ پاسخ داد: «نه. هیچ تردیدی ندارم.» او افزود اگر روند اوضاع تغییر کند، آماده اقدام است.

رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا مدعی شد واشنگتن کنترل کامل تنگه هرمز را در اختیار دارد و میزان خروج نفت از منطقه از پیش از جنگ بیشتر شده است. او همچنین ادعا کرد آمریکا طی پنج ماه گذشته سربازی از دست نداده است.

آقای هویت سپس پرسید آیا ترامپ حاضر است محاصره را حتی برای ۲۶ ماه، تا فروپاشی حکومت ایران، ادامه دهد. آقای ترامپ تعهد زمانی مشخصی نداد؛ در عوض، با طرح ادعاهایی درباره تورم، پرداخت‌نشدن حقوق سربازان و نابودی توان نظامی ایران، فشار موجود را مؤثر توصیف کرد.

او در پاسخ به پرسشی درباره باقی ماندن حاکمان کنونی ایران تا پایان ریاست‌جمهوری‌اش، گفت: «بله، این شکست خواهد بود.»

آقای هویت پرسید اگر ایران یک مقام ارشد آمریکایی را بکشد، چه اتفاقی خواهد افتاد. آقای ترامپ تهدید کرد: «دیگر مدت زیادی دوام نخواهند آورد.»

دونالد ترامپ از جی‌دی ونس خواسته است توجه خود را از مذاکرات ایران به مسائل داخلی آمریکا معطوف کند. آقای ترامپ معاونش را مأمور تمرکز بر ادعاهای فساد و جرم در شهرها و ایالت‌های تحت اداره دموکرات‌ها کرده است.

این دستور در حالی صادر شد که آقای ونس در تلاش برای دستیابی به آتش‌بسی تازه و ازسرگیری مذاکرات هسته‌ای نقش داشت. تحلیل‌گران تغییر مأموریت او را در پیوند با ارزیابی صریحش از شکست انتخاباتی جمهوری‌خواهان بررسی می‌کند؛ آقای ونس جنگ ایران را عامل این شکست دانسته بود.

واشنگتن‌پست این تحول را نشانه ترجیح ادامه محاصره دریایی و فشار اقتصادی بر تلاش برای توافق توصیف می‌کند. به ادعای این روزنامه، آقای ونس برای بررسی امکان بازگشایی تنگه هرمز و محدود کردن برنامه هسته‌ای ایران، با تندروهای حکومت ایران تماس گرفته بود.

این روزنامه تأکید می‌کند که هنوز روشن نیست آقای ترامپ تمامی تلاش‌های دیپلماتیک را متوقف کرده باشد. تغییر مأموریت معاون رئیس‌جمهور، برای متحدان آمریکا در خلیج فارس نیز ابهام ایجاد کرده است؛ کشورهایی که خواهان حفظ مسیر مذاکرات‌اند و نگران پیامدهای تداوم رویارویی و فشار اقتصادی بدون دستیابی به راه‌حلی سیاسی هستند.

سی‌ان‌ان در گزارشی، سخنان دونالد ترامپ درباره ایران را حاوی پیام‌های متناقض توصیف می‌کند. رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا ابتدا در تروث سوشال اعلام کرد نیازی به توافق با تهران ندارد و از جی‌دی ونس خواست توجه خود را بر مسائل داخلی متمرکز کند؛ اما بعد در مصاحبه با هیو هویت، باقی ماندن حکومت کنونی ایران تا پایان ریاست‌جمهوری‌اش را «شکست» دانست.

به گزارش این شبکه، آقای ترامپ در همان مصاحبه احتمال اقدام نظامی دوباره را نیز مطرح کرد، هرچند هم‌زمان گفت ضرورتی برای استفاده از نیروی نظامی نمی‌بیند. سی‌ان‌ان این اظهارات را کنار مواضع اخیر او قرار می‌دهد که از بی‌میلی به تشدید درگیری حکایت داشت.

این گزارش همچنین به موقعیت سیاسی آقای ونس می‌پردازد. معاون رئیس‌جمهور که مذاکرات را هدایت می‌کرد، پیش‌تر جنگ را عامل شکست انتخاباتی جمهوری‌خواهان معرفی کرده بود. سی‌ان‌ان می‌نویسد کنار رفتن از این پرونده می‌تواند برای او، با توجه به احتمال نامزدی در انتخابات ۲۰۲۸، از نظر سیاسی سودمند باشد.

این شبکه یادآوری می‌کند که تغییر مأموریت آقای ونس زمانی اعلام شد که تلاش‌های دیپلماتیک برای جلوگیری از بازگشت به جنگ تمام‌عیار شدت گرفته بود. گزارش، تغییر لحن آقای ترامپ را برجسته می‌کند، اما از تصمیم قطعی او برای آغاز حملات تازه یا تغییر حکومت ایران خبر نمی‌دهد.

بلومبرگ می‌نویسد دونالد ترامپ رویکرد تازه‌ای را بررسی می‌کند: باقی گذاشتن جنگ ایران در وضعیتی بلاتکلیف و فاصله گرفتن از تلاش برای حل‌وفصل جامع آن. دستور او به جی‌دی ونس برای تمرکز بر مسایل داخل کشور، احتمال پایان درگیری بدون توافق بر سر محدودیت‌های هسته‌ای را مطرح کرده؛ همان موضوعی که توجیه اصلی آغاز جنگ معرفی می‌شد.

به نوشته این رسانه، شکست جمهوری‌خواهان در انتخابات، هزینه سیاسی جنگ را آشکار کرده است. اکنون، در کنار تشدید حملات یا افزایش فشار برای گرفتن امتیاز، پذیرش بن‌بست نیز مطرح شده است.

نیت سوانسون، مقام پیشین آمریکایی، معتقد است دولت گزینه مطلوبی ندارد: اقدام نظامی خطر تشدید درگیری دارد و چشم‌انداز توافق مناسب نیز ضعیف است. در مقابل، یک مقام کاخ سفید، محاصره، تحریم‌ها و عملیات «دروازه آهنین» را نشانه قدرت موقعیت واشنگتن می‌داند.

گزارش هشدار می‌دهد ادامه این وضعیت می‌تواند متحدان خلیج فارس را مقابل ایرانی جسورتر، بدون مسیر روشن ثبات، باقی بگذارد

دونالد ترامپ می‌گوید عربستان سعودی، قطر و دیگر کشورهای خلیج فارس از او خواسته‌اند فعلاً از حملات گسترده‌تر به ایران خودداری کند و وضعیت کنونی را ادامه دهد. رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا در مصاحبه با استیون ای اسمیت در کاخ سفید، مدعی شد می‌تواند به جنگ فوراً پایان دهد، اما به درخواست متحدان منطقه‌ای، فشار اقتصادی و نظامی را حفظ کرده است.

رول‌کال همچنین ادعای رئیس‌جمهور درباره کنترل تنگه هرمز را در کنار وضعیت این آبراه قرار می‌دهد. گزارش می‌نویسد هرمز همچنان محل مناقشه و برای کشتی‌های تجاری خطرناک است و مقام‌های ایرانی نیز مدعی کنترل بخش عمده آن هستند.

این رسانه تغییر مأموریت آقای ونس به پیگیری ادعاهای فساد در مناطق تحت اداره دموکرات‌ها را تلاشی احتمالی برای جلب رضایت دوباره رأی‌دهندگان جمهوری‌خواه می‌داند. با این حال، اعلام بی‌نیازی از توافق، به‌خودی‌خود پاسخ روشنی به خواست پایان جنگ نمی‌دهد؛ به‌ویژه وقتی ناامنی کشتیرانی و هزینه‌های اقتصادی درگیری همچنان ادامه دارد.

واشنگتن‌پست در گزارش خود، دستور ترامپ به ونس را نشانه عقب‌نشینی از تلاش برای توافق و ترجیح ادامه محاصره دریایی و فشار اقتصادی توصیف می‌کند. به نوشته این روزنامه، آقای ونس برای بررسی امکان پایان مذاکره‌شده درگیری، با تندروهای حکومت ایران وارد تماس شده بود.

آکسیوس نیز این تصمیم را با تغییر اولویت سیاسی آقای ونس پیوند می‌دهد: معاون رئیس‌جمهور، پس از نسبت دادن شکست انتخاباتی جمهوری‌خواهان به جنگ، اکنون مأمور تمرکز بر ادعاهای فساد در شهرها و ایالت‌های دموکرات شده است.

این رسانه می‌نویسد پیام آقای ترامپ بار دیگر عدم‌اطمینان را به بازارهایی بازگرداند که پایان جنگ را نزدیک تصور می‌کردند؛ قیمت نفت افزایش یافت و سهام افت کرد. آکسیوس همچنین یادآوری می‌کند آقای ونس اخیراً در تلاش برای آتش‌بسی تازه و ازسرگیری مذاکرات هسته‌ای نقش پررنگی داشت.

پرسشی که از کنار هم قرار دادن این دو گزارش شکل می‌گیرد، این است: آیا توقف تلاش علنی برای توافق، تصمیمی پایدار است یا مرحله دیگری از سیاست متغیر واشنگتن؟ هیچ‌یک پاسخ قطعی ارائه نمی‌کنند.

دونالد ترامپ در مصاحبه با هیو هویت، مجری محافظه‌کار آمریکایی، گفت برای استفاده دوباره از نیروی نظامی علیه ایران «هیچ تردیدی» ندارد و باقی ماندن حکومت کنونی ایران تا پایان ریاست‌جمهوری خود را «شکست» می‌داند.

این دو موضع، در کنار اعلام بی‌نیازی واشنگتن از توافق با تهران، پرسش درباره هدف نهایی آمریکا و چگونگی پایان جنگ را به محور پوشش رسانه‌های آمریکایی تبدیل کرده است.

واشنگتن‌پست و آکسیوس، دستور آقای ترامپ به جی‌دی ونس برای تمرکز بر مسائل داخلی را نشانه عقب‌نشینی از مسیر توافق و ترجیح ادامه فشار اقتصادی توصیف کرده‌اند؛ بلومبرگ نیز این رویکرد را شرط‌بندی بر دوام وضعیتی شکننده می‌داند و هشدار می‌دهد پذیرش بن‌بست، لزوماً به پایان درگیری یا رفع خطر جنگی تازه منجر نخواهد شد.

دونالد ترامپ در مصاحبه با هیو هویت، استفاده دوباره از نیروی نظامی علیه ایران را منتفی ندانست. آقای هویت پرسید آیا برای جلوگیری از تهدید متحدان و کشتی‌های آمریکایی تردید خواهد کرد؛ آقای ترامپ پاسخ داد: «نه. هیچ تردیدی ندارم.» او افزود اگر روند اوضاع تغییر کند، آماده اقدام است.

رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا مدعی شد واشنگتن کنترل کامل تنگه هرمز را در اختیار دارد و میزان خروج نفت از منطقه از پیش از جنگ بیشتر شده است. او همچنین ادعا کرد آمریکا طی پنج ماه گذشته سربازی از دست نداده است.

آقای هویت سپس پرسید آیا ترامپ حاضر است محاصره را حتی برای ۲۶ ماه، تا فروپاشی حکومت ایران، ادامه دهد. آقای ترامپ تعهد زمانی مشخصی نداد؛ در عوض، با طرح ادعاهایی درباره تورم، پرداخت‌نشدن حقوق سربازان و نابودی توان نظامی ایران، فشار موجود را مؤثر توصیف کرد.

او در پاسخ به پرسشی درباره باقی ماندن حاکمان کنونی ایران تا پایان ریاست‌جمهوری‌اش، گفت: «بله، این شکست خواهد بود.»

آقای هویت پرسید اگر ایران یک مقام ارشد آمریکایی را بکشد، چه اتفاقی خواهد افتاد. آقای ترامپ تهدید کرد: «دیگر مدت زیادی دوام نخواهند آورد.»

دونالد ترامپ از جی‌دی ونس خواسته است توجه خود را از مذاکرات ایران به مسائل داخلی آمریکا معطوف کند. آقای ترامپ معاونش را مأمور تمرکز بر ادعاهای فساد و جرم در شهرها و ایالت‌های تحت اداره دموکرات‌ها کرده است.

این دستور در حالی صادر شد که آقای ونس در تلاش برای دستیابی به آتش‌بسی تازه و ازسرگیری مذاکرات هسته‌ای نقش داشت. تحلیل‌گران تغییر مأموریت او را در پیوند با ارزیابی صریحش از شکست انتخاباتی جمهوری‌خواهان بررسی می‌کند؛ آقای ونس جنگ ایران را عامل این شکست دانسته بود.

واشنگتن‌پست این تحول را نشانه ترجیح ادامه محاصره دریایی و فشار اقتصادی بر تلاش برای توافق توصیف می‌کند. به ادعای این روزنامه، آقای ونس برای بررسی امکان بازگشایی تنگه هرمز و محدود کردن برنامه هسته‌ای ایران، با تندروهای حکومت ایران تماس گرفته بود.

این روزنامه تأکید می‌کند که هنوز روشن نیست آقای ترامپ تمامی تلاش‌های دیپلماتیک را متوقف کرده باشد. تغییر مأموریت معاون رئیس‌جمهور، برای متحدان آمریکا در خلیج فارس نیز ابهام ایجاد کرده است؛ کشورهایی که خواهان حفظ مسیر مذاکرات‌اند و نگران پیامدهای تداوم رویارویی و فشار اقتصادی بدون دستیابی به راه‌حلی سیاسی هستند.

به گزارش این شبکه، آقای ترامپ در همان مصاحبه احتمال اقدام نظامی دوباره را نیز مطرح کرد، هرچند هم‌زمان گفت ضرورتی برای استفاده از نیروی نظامی نمی‌بیند. سی‌ان‌ان این اظهارات را کنار مواضع اخیر او قرار می‌دهد که از بی‌میلی به تشدید درگیری حکایت داشت.

این گزارش همچنین به موقعیت سیاسی آقای ونس می‌پردازد. معاون رئیس‌جمهور که مذاکرات را هدایت می‌کرد، پیش‌تر جنگ را عامل شکست انتخاباتی جمهوری‌خواهان معرفی کرده بود. سی‌ان‌ان می‌نویسد کنار رفتن از این پرونده می‌تواند برای او، با توجه به احتمال نامزدی در انتخابات ۲۰۲۸، از نظر سیاسی سودمند باشد.

رول‌کال همچنین ادعای رئیس‌جمهور درباره کنترل تنگه هرمز را در کنار وضعیت این آبراه قرار می‌دهد. گزارش می‌نویسد هرمز همچنان محل مناقشه و برای کشتی‌های تجاری خطرناک است و مقام‌های ایرانی نیز مدعی کنترل بخش عمده آن هستند.

این رسانه تغییر مأموریت آقای ونس به پیگیری ادعاهای فساد در مناطق تحت اداره دموکرات‌ها را تلاشی احتمالی برای جلب رضایت دوباره رأی‌دهندگان جمهوری‌خواه می‌داند. با این حال، اعلام بی‌نیازی از توافق، به‌خودی‌خود پاسخ روشنی به خواست پایان جنگ نمی‌دهد؛ به‌ویژه وقتی ناامنی کشتیرانی و هزینه‌های اقتصادی درگیری همچنان ادامه دارد.

واشنگتن‌پست در گزارش خود، دستور ترامپ به ونس را نشانه عقب‌نشینی از تلاش برای توافق و ترجیح ادامه محاصره دریایی و فشار اقتصادی توصیف می‌کند. به نوشته این روزنامه، آقای ونس برای بررسی امکان پایان مذاکره‌شده درگیری، با تندروهای حکومت ایران وارد تماس شده بود.

گزارش تأکید می‌کند که تغییر موضع آقای ترامپ، ابهام برای متحدان آمریکا در خلیج فارس را افزایش داده است. این کشورها برای حفظ مذاکرات تلاش کرده‌اند و نگران پیامدهای ادامه رویارویی هستند. واشنگتن‌پست تصریح می‌کند هنوز روشن نیست رئیس‌جمهور دیپلماسی را کاملاً کنار گذاشته باشد.

آکسیوس نیز این تصمیم را با تغییر اولویت سیاسی آقای ونس پیوند می‌دهد: معاون رئیس‌جمهور، پس از نسبت دادن شکست انتخاباتی جمهوری‌خواهان به جنگ، اکنون مأمور تمرکز بر ادعاهای فساد در شهرها و ایالت‌های دموکرات شده است.

این رسانه می‌نویسد پیام آقای ترامپ بار دیگر عدم‌اطمینان را به بازارهایی بازگرداند که پایان جنگ را نزدیک تصور می‌کردند؛ قیمت نفت افزایش یافت و سهام افت کرد. آکسیوس همچنین یادآوری می‌کند آقای ونس اخیراً در تلاش برای آتش‌بسی تازه و ازسرگیری مذاکرات هسته‌ای نقش پررنگی داشت.

پرسشی که از کنار هم قرار دادن این دو گزارش شکل می‌گیرد، این است: آیا توقف تلاش علنی برای توافق، تصمیمی پایدار است یا مرحله دیگری از سیاست متغیر واشنگتن؟ هیچ‌یک پاسخ قطعی ارائه نمی‌کنند.
